body:
Found while reviewing #476. **Blocking #476.** The retirement of the old service/environment model wasn't finished. This supersedes items 1–3 of #477.

## Problem
#476 removes the old service API. But the older environment model still works alongside `OrchestratorBackend`, still carrying URL-returning service settings that no longer do anything:

- `gimbal environment start/stop` and the Docker environment plugin (`plugins/docker`) provision environments with their own `Start`/`Stop` receipts and return direct HTTP `Execution`. This is a second model of "environment" that sits outside `OrchestratorBackend`.
- `taskdaemon.Daemon.PublicHost` is set (`cmd/gimbal/daemon.go`) but never read, because its only reader `Daemon.service` was deleted.
- The Docker plugin still validates and publishes `ServicePorts`/`PublicHost` ("published services require PublicHost reachable by their consumer").
- The `gimbal environment` help text still describes "URL-returning services", "Start means launched, not ready; workflows check readiness", and "scope cleanup releases services". All of this contradicts the contract.
- **`Route.Environment` changed meaning without updating its callers.** It used to be a display label; now any non-empty value switches on orchestrated placement. `internal/host/routes.go:111` still writes the task endpoint URL into it. `runner.go:48` and `effects.Call` then refuse the run, so `--workflow-endpoint` plus `--task-endpoint` no longer works.
- **Execution-route daemons have no `SecretsBackend`.** `serveEnvironmentOptions` (`gimbal daemon`, used by Docker) and the registered `local` backend build `taskdaemon.New()` without `Secrets`. On those routes, `WithYields` with names and `WithRequirements` fail mid-run instead of being rejected up front or supported.

## Done when
- The Docker/`gimbal environment` path either **becomes an `OrchestratorBackend`** (Docker starts a scope-assigned daemon that work reaches through messaging) or **is deleted**, together with its docs. No separate environment model remains.
- `PublicHost`, `ServicePorts` and the URL-service help text are gone.
- `Route.Environment` has one meaning, and every caller that writes it follows that meaning. Any separate placement label gets its own field.
- Every route that accepts `WithYields`/`WithRequirements` has a secrets backend. Routes that can't support them reject them before any native work starts.
title: Finish retiring the old environment/service model (Docker environments, PublicHost, Route.Environment)
